notes: College of Arts and Humanities' Jewish Studies Four Year Academic Plan, Track Two (Language Enhanced). The source PDF's term grid converts to garbled, column-interleaved text (the by-term grid and the separate requirements-checklist table run together), so exact per-slot Fall/Spring placement could not be reliably reconstructed; flagged in docs/project/owner-review.md. Term placement here follows the plan's legible signals (JWST187/171 in Year 1, Foundations courses across Years 1-2, JWST409/ISRL448 -- the Capstone -- in Year 4, and the Language Enhanced Track's Hebrew 3xx-4xx/Area of Emphasis/electives in Years 3-4 as the plan lists them) and otherwise spreads the remaining major requirements across Years 2-4 in plan order. Gen Ed and general-elective slots are left out: only the major is audited.
Big Question filled with JWST171, named directly by the catalog and the plan.
Foundations (three courses from at least two areas) filled with JWST233 (History), ISRL282 (Literature and/or Film), and JWST262 (Thought, Culture, and/or Religion), all named by the catalog.
Capstone filled with ISRL448, named directly by the catalog and the plan.

Hebrew or Yiddish 3XX-4XX (six credits) filled with HEBR313 and HEBR314 (Conversation and Composition I/II), real UMD Hebrew courses confirmed by program-sources/hebrew-minor.md and program-sources/israel-studies-minor.md already in this codebase (the catalog and plan for this major name only 'Hebrew or Yiddish 3XX-4XX level', no specific course numbers).

Area of Emphasis (nine credits at the 300-400 level) filled with JWST319, JWST324, and JWST325, real JWST courses from the Academic Catalog's approved-course list, chosen only to satisfy the level/credit shape (no per-area upper-level list is published; see Program reviewNotes).
In-Major Electives (three courses in Jewish Studies) filled with JWST234, JWST235, and JWST256, all real JWST courses from the Academic Catalog's approved-course list.
